algorithm: XOR stream cipher with SHA-256 counter-mode keystream

classes.desc: XOR stream cipher over a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream.
classes.name: StreamCipher

complexity: O(n) per encrypt/decrypt of n bytes
data_flow_ascii:
--key or --seed -> derive_key (SHA-256)
key + counter -> keystream (SHA-256 blocks)
plaintext XOR keystream -> ciphertext hex
ciphertext XOR keystream -> plaintext (round trip)
description_sentence: Encrypts and decrypts data with a hand-written XOR stream cipher using a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream.
failure_note: Decryption with the wrong key or corrupted hex yields garbage rather than an error, which is expected for a raw stream cipher with no authentication tag; --decrypt validates hex before decoding.

functions.desc: Derive a 32-byte key from --key text, or from the seed by default.
functions.name: derive_key

functions.desc: SHA-256 counter-mode keystream of exactly `length` bytes.
functions.name: keystream

functions.desc: Decrypt bytes; XOR is its own inverse.
functions.name: StreamCipher.decrypt

functions.desc: Parse args; round-trip demo, or one-shot --encrypt/--decrypt.
functions.name: main

label: Encryption tool
output_shape: The default run prints plaintext, ciphertext hex, recovered text, and a MATCH/MISMATCH verdict; --encrypt/--decrypt print just the result.
pitch_sentence: A {topic} encryption tool in pure Python with a hand-written SHA-256 stream cipher that proves itself with an encrypt/decrypt round trip.

qa.a: Yes; XOR is its own inverse, so decrypt simply re-applies encrypt with the same keystream.
qa.q: Is decryption the same operation as encryption?

qa.a: It is a demonstration cipher, not audited cryptography; it shows the construction honestly but should not protect real secrets.
Yes: --encrypt TEXT prints hex, and --decrypt HEX prints the recovered text, both using the same --key/--seed.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} encryption tool in Python (stdlib hashlib) implementing an XOR stream cipher with a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream; demo performs a full encrypt/decrypt round trip and verifies the result.
run_notes: Use `--encrypt TEXT` / `--decrypt HEX` for one-shot operations with --key.
scaling_note: Keystream generation is O(n) in message length with small constant overhead; fine for kilobyte-to-megabyte demo payloads.
storage_note: In-memory only: keys, keystream, and messages exist for the run; nothing is written to disk.
tradeoff_note: A raw stream cipher is simple and dependency-free but provides no authentication; real use would need an AEAD construction.
